reviews.text: It was great experience eating here
Amazing place! At first we didn’t see anybody inside so we were worried that it might not be good but don’t worry, this is amazing food with great service!

Really good and affordable dim sum. The waitress needs a raise. She was so attentive but not overbearing. The food was great! Some things exceeded expectations and some things met expectations, but nothing was bad! Would probably make some different choices next time, but I’m happy with our experience. We left full, and that’s all I can ask for. Will definitely be coming back
10/10 experience, great, hotpot, sushi, beverages; great service, will be back soon!!
I went here, and then I saw a rodent run across the floor. I was startled by this and then left afterwards. Very unfortunate…

This is my first hot pot. We went on the early side, 6pm on a Thursday and it was not too crowded. The maitre d' and servers were very nice to help us order since we weren't familiar with the menu. I had the fish maw chicken, which was very chicken, and my wife had the pork broth. There is an important step to dressing the broth from the dressing bar. I added chili oil, and my wife added garlic, salt and hoisin. I loved ordering the bullfrog legs, black tripe, and pork brain! My wife ordered beef shoulder and beef slices and everything was delicious. There is also a raw bar with mussels, clams, and whole shrimp that I partook of and I can report it was fresh and delicious.

The food here was SO good! We went as a group of four and shared a hot pot with two different broths, tom yum and mushroom. Then we got shrimp, different meats, mushrooms, noodles and other things to cook in the broths. Honestly, food was a 10/10 for us. Everything was really tasty and it was also such a fun meal to share with friends.

Service was good. Nothing particularly extraordinary, but we had no problems at all and everything worked well for what we needed.

The atmosphere is also really nice and the restaurant is right in the middle of Chinatown. It does get pretty busy though, so I would definitely call ahead to make a reservation.

Really good food and such a fun experience to do with a group!

Good service, good value and, if you like hotpot, really great food. Some of the most authentic Chinese food we’ve had outside of China.

Extremely disappointing experience as a tourist. We ordered the pork belly skewers, but they did not look or taste right at all. When we politely asked to exchange them for something else, our waiter immediately gave us an attitude. Instead of resolving the issue, he actually brought out raw pork belly to our table to argue that it was "good," then cleared our plates and completely ignored us.

We had to flag him down again, only for him to walk away while we were mid-sentence. Instead of finishing our service, he handed our check off to another staff member to bring to us—even though we weren't even done ordering. We were met with dirty looks from the staff the entire time. A terrible way to treat customers. I would not recommend this place.

Overrated! We ordered the $43 buffet. And still need to pay $6.99 additional for snowflake beef. But the beef is not as good as I had in other hot pot places. In general, all the lamb and beef are not impressive. You can get the same quality food with much cheaper price in other places. The beverage options are very limited.

Definitely my favorite hotpot place in NYC!! I didn’t expect it to be good because it is in Little Italy (haha!) but man the quality of the food was just soooo gooood and the service was attentive. Love this place! Highly recommend!

Great spot for all-you-can-eat individual hot pot in Chinatown. I really like the setup where everyone gets their own pot, so you can choose your own broth and cook everything exactly how you like it.

There are several broth options, including Chongqing spicy, tomato, mushroom, Tom Yum, green peppercorn, and more. The AYCE selection has a good variety of meats, seafood, vegetables, noodles, and hot pot staples. You can easily mix and match depending on what you’re craving.

The Classic AYCE is $28, while the House Special is $43 with more premium options. For Chinatown, I think it’s a pretty solid value, especially if you come hungry.

Good option for a casual hot pot meal with friends when everyone wants their own flavor and pace.

We thought this was an AYCE dim sum, hot pot and skewer place as the name suggests, however, we found out ONLY the hot pot is included in the $43 price.

With tips and tax, it's around $56/pp, which I find not as not the best value for JUST hot pot, considering there are much better ayce options elsewhere and with much bigger selection of food of food and seafood. Even a decent seafood buffet that serves unlimited snow crab legs and sashimi is around $38/pp only..

That aside, food tasted mostly fine, with 2 questionable items for freshness (1 round of shrimp paste and 1 round of cilantro meatballs, tasted off and we just spit it out after tasting.

The guy who served us was fine, but a different guy gave us the bill.  The tip was ALREADY added for us in the total at an amount higher than what I had calculated. It was almost $60 for just the tip. When i asked the guy what % it was, he said "20%," but when I showed him the calculation on my phone, it was a diff amount in the mid 40s.  Turns out, he had calculated the tip based on total including tax, instead of just the food. Tip should not include tax amount. Then he just grabbed the bill from my hand without saying anything and came back with a new bill with an adjusted amount. I found his attitude kinda rude and definitely left a sour taste in our mouths.

Note to owner: Tips should be earned, not imposed. I don't think a restaurant should IMPOSE an automatic 20% tip for the customer. The tip should always be selected by the customer to reflect the actual service based on their experience. For that reason and the overall "value" of the meal, we are NOT likely to be returning customers.

We recently had lunch at Easy Joy and I am quite surprised by the reviews vs the experience. 

I'll start off by saying that the food was pretty good! We were satisfied with what we ordered, it was more so the model/service that was disappointing. I would honesty say that this is the spirit airlines of Dim Sum. I opted to do A La Carte since I wasn't hungry enough to justify AYCE, and they let us know that if we were "caught"  sharing food, it would be an additional charge. That was fine since I had no interest in meat. We are very familiar with AYCE service so that was fine, but the manner that things were displayed were very off putting. Someone quite literally stood at the end of the table watching... it was awkward. Service was very slow and when food was placed on the table we were not told what it was, which was awkward since we were sharing a table with people and their food was being given to us and vice versa. The area of the restaurant is nice and located directly in little Italy. 

The shrimp spring rolls and crap Shanghai dumping were great!
All you can eat dim sum no longer available. Misleading is not cool . Staffs are pleasant but have no idea about serving business.. over a disappointing experience

Tried this place on a weekday around 5 I was able to get a seat without waiting. They have a big variety of things and some stuff I haven't seen at other hotpots. They also have all you can drink sodas and desserts. I had the mushroom broth which was delicious had a nice flavor. The meats you have to order from the servers who are friendly and constantly checking if you need anything. I wish there were more non soda options for the drinks like coconut juice or other Asian drinks but they do have diet and ice tea. The desserts are good and small so you can try more without being wasteful.

This place ROCKS! I'm already planning my next trip back. Went on a weekday for dinner with four friends, and had no trouble snagging a same-day reservation (there was also plenty of open seating around us). The interior is spacious, with plenty of seating, and clean. Everyone gets their own personal hot pot -- only downside of this is you can't split your broth between a spicy broth AND a bone broth (as is my wont), so I ordered a bone broth and my partner ordered a spicy broth and we switched halfway through. 

The menu is huge: about half the items on the AYCE menu (mainly cuts of red meat), you have to order from the waiter, and the other half (incl. veggies, noodles, fish and beef balls, tofu, etc.) you can help yourself to in a stocked fridge area. This is the stuff of AYCE dreams. We got all sorts of fish, so much meat (beef, pork belly, lamb, you name it), giant shrimp heads, frog legs, seaweed, bamboo, lotus root, all kinds of veggies, etc. etc. etc. We also loaded up on sweet potato noodles, fish tofu, actual tofu, fish balls, beef balls, fish balls stuffed WITH beef, delicious tiny fried mantou that you dip in condensed milk... they even had ciba cake, which is a fave and kind of a rare find! It was a joyous, dizzying experience, and that's before you even get to the dessert bar (full of tiny cakes, cannolis, various puddings of all flavors!). 

Service is very attentive -- the waiters refilled our broths often. I can't say much else except that this is probably my new go-to hot pot place. Everything was delicious and fresh, and for ~$50/person, it's hard to find better value elsewhere.

AYCE Level: Expert. Regret Level: Zero. 
​Just rolled out of Easy Joy Dim Sum & AYCE Hot Pot in Little Italy, and let's just say the "All You Can Eat" part was taken as a personal challenge. If you're looking to feast like a king without the royal price tag, this is the spot.
​The Breakdown:
​The Broth Game: I went with the GuangDong Fish Maw Chicken. We're talking Emperor Chicken, red dates, and goji berries. This isn't just soup; it's a soul-warming masterpiece. Best part? When they refill it, they use the actual broth, not just plain water. The flavor stays 100% until the very last dip.
​The Heavy Hitters: For the meat lovers, the New Zealand baby lamb and beef tongue are top-tier. But if you're here for the real deal, they've got the delicacies: Duck feet, frog legs, beef omasum, and yes--pig brains. If you know, you know. 
​The "Secret" Strategy: You can order fresh Dim Sum at a fraction of the cost if you're doing hot pot. Pro tip: Snag those warm pineapple pork buns the second you see them. They go fast for a reason. 
​The Vibes: Surprisingly spacious seating (no elbowing your neighbor for the last shrimp ball) and a massive fridge full of veggies and unlimited soft drinks.
​The Finish Line: They've got everything from mango pudding to... cannolis. Because it's Little Italy, and why wouldn't you want a cannoli after a hot pot marathon? 
​The Intel:  Price: Around $51--insane value for the quality.
 Discounts: Senior and Military/Veteran discounts available.
‍ Service: Our waiter was a legend, constantly checking in to make sure the table was stocked.
 Warning: It gets packed. Call for a reservation unless you enjoy staring at other people eating through the window.
​Overall, 10/10. My belt is screaming, but my heart is full. Can't wait to go back and do it all over again.

I came here for my birthday and had a great experience. They offer both hot pot and dim sum, with a great selection of options to choose from. The ambiance is really nice and makes it a great place to celebrate or gather with friends.

Our server, Hao, was very attentive and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal.

I especially liked that they have a dessert selection. The mango pudding and rose pudding were both delicious and a perfect way to end the meal. They also have a great variety of sodas to choose from.

Overall, it's a great spot for groups and I really enjoyed the variety of food options available.
Andrew is an exceptional host! The tomy soup was so flavorful. It had the cutest ambiance with great music! Will go here again !
Absolutely great. I love everything about it. Soooooooo good. They only thing they need more help at the front door.

Good!

Good taste some  and steaks

Noodles and egg  chopsticks and broth.

Chili peppers
this was definetly a 10/10 experience ! loved it so much ! next time i'm in new york i'm definetly coming back !
Came all the way from California and tried this. Superrrrrr yummmmy ! Need to come back next time I visit :)

First of all, don't be put off by the price per person if you're from out of town. It's definitely worth it. We each got our own pot, ordered a boat load of meat per round (no limit), and got our veggies and mushrooms from the buffet area. The non-alcoholic beverages were included and they also don't charge for leftover meat. A dream come true for any AYCE hot pot lover.

This was probably our favorite spot on our NYC trip, and it definitely felt like we got our money's worth. I think there could be more variety of meat and seafood but it wasn't something that would take away from my experience.

Dim Sum is awful. Served lukewarm and flavorless. Their mini pan fried buns are shameful. They are the size of a quarter coin and tasted like machine mass produced frozen market goods. The meat in it is gross. Sampan congee has no flavor. It came with stale/freezer burn flavor seafood meats and stale peanuts. 

Service there is a joke. They're a bunch of kids busy goofing around, dropping plates, and unprofessionally chatting away while carrying out trays of food from the kitchen. I wouldn't want my server to be talking on top of my food.

Don't know where the positive reviews are coming from. For a true dim sum experience, this is NOT the place for it. Definitely will NOT be returning and NOT "easy joy".

I took my friend here for her birthday! She loves dim sum. I originally thought it was an all-you-can-eat dim sum place, but they discontinued that. I usually like to try the beef noodles. I thought it was very good. The noodles are soft, and the beef is tasty.

Absolutely loved this place. I haven't been to an all you can eat in a while. Never tried hot pot and im glad I did. Very filling and you definitely get your money's worth. The desserts you get with the deal are pretty good too.
It was so delicious!!! The staff was welcoming and attentive! Food was yummy and they even offered us free dessert. Nice treat in NYC!

I never write reviews but this place had such delicious food. It was so delectable, i would drive from california to here if i was craving it. The service was good, and all people who served us were kind and didnt mess up. The restaurant was well decorated and was cozy, it was a nice place to be in. Overall, this place is so good!!!!! 1000000/10, go!!!!!!!

Loved this spot. Honestly one of my faves for hot pot and dim sum. Came here a while back the and staff was super nice and food was quick to come by. Ordered a variety of food like fatty beef, truffle dumplings, soup dumplings, etc.

The place can be pretty busy and lively  so I do suggest making a reservation in advance.

Ambiance (4/5): The establishment has several available tables for the hot pot service.
Service (4/5): We ended up waiting for 25 minutes to be seated (walk-in) and were annoyed because the whole time there were empty tables (I'm talking like 40% of the restaurant was empty). I'm sure they were being held for reservations but didn't like how it was being handled despite having our full party waiting.
The restaurant is understaffed because there were only a few on the floor able to take orders from all the tables. When we were seated, it took forever to get our soup orders in. However, when one of our friends ordered the mala, they didn't charge extra for switching to the pork.
For those that can't handle spice, warning that the mala option was way too spicy even for me. It was a hair too spicy that I couldn't quite enjoy the meal without having to clear my sinuses or eat as quickly as I can so the numbness didn't set in haha
Some meat cuts were definitely more premium than others but once ordered, we definitely got our money's worth. After tip/tax, it was $55/pp. The selection of AYCE veggies was great. Th dessert bar was extensive and bite size that you could try them all. They even have mini pineapple buns and egg tarts!! Sad that they ran out of the egg tarts when I was ready to have them. Additionally, the soft drink selection was HUGE of varieties of diet and regular, teas, etc.

Hotpot is very standard. Dim sum is cheap w the AYCE option but imo didn't taste good. They don't take ressies so we waited over an hour. Wasn't worth the wait. So many better hotpot options in the area.

Great place to grab lunch! We went on a. Friday it wasn't too packed and was $43/pp for AYCE hotpot. They no longer have the AYCE dim sum option. Wide variety of food to pick from even off the menu as they have three showcases with more things like vegetables noodles rice cakes desserts etc. Servers were attentive and nice. And the sodas are included!!

Very big place and has a good variety of vegetables and meats to choose from. The desserts were simple, but still had a good selection to choose from. Our waiter was very clear with the menu and did not push us to leave even after 90 minutes. They handed us the bill so we got the message, but did not rush us. The hot pot was a bit pricey compared to other spots, but overall, a decent place.

The appeal of a hotpot restaurant in downtown Manhattan that is comparable to the plethora of choices found in Flushing cannot be understated. The various options for broth and cuts of meats and seafood are both favorable and fresh.  Self-served veggies and fish/meatballs can fill you easily without ordering any premium items!  Unfortunately dim sum is no longer part of the AYCE promotion, but it surely hasn't dampened the visits to Easy Joy since.   

The aesthetic is also a nice nostalgic touch with a decor resembling traditional Chinese dim sum banquet restaurants.  The staff is also very friendly and multilingual which adds to the experience as well.

Was craving hotpot and stumbled upon this spot. Definitely amazed by the amount of variety we have. My boyfriend and I did the Hot Pot AYCE where each of us got to pick a broth of our choice served in a small pot. Then we got to order a variety of fresh cut meat, seafood, snacks which the staffs will bring from the back. There are also dessert stations, sauce stations, and other ingredient stations like veggies and hot pot materials like fish balls that you can help yourself to. 

We definitely like the wide variety but the food taste overall just ok. Service was a little slow since we didn't get our utensils, cups of water, and apron later on. The vibes were also interesting at this place where since it's situated in Little Italy, there is definitely a lot of tourists.

Well priced and the quality of most of the meat was pretty great. The desserts at the end were pretty fire as well. Decor wise this clearly used to be an Italian restaurant, as they have several posters of Italy still up -- giving it that classic Sichuan rustic charm

Was initially a little skeptical about going to a dim sum location in the middle of Little Italy. But man this place is incredible. They told us they no longer offer the all you can eat option for dim sum. So we ended up getting al la carte plates. This was our best and most affordable meal our entire trip. I have to say the eggrolls were truly incredible. We ate two plates and seriously considered a third. Everything was made fresh and had care in its creation. Our server was incredibly kind and helpful. my only complaint is I wish they had a location in Phoenix. If you were looking for affordable and amazing dim sum in New York City, I would highly recommend Easy Joy.

I came here for dinner for an event recently and had an amazing time. Located in Little Italy, this AYCE hot pot spot is a great cozy meal on a cold day. Service here is great and the restaurant is spacious.

Their dim sum here is pretty solid and I would say that their hot pot is pretty high-quality. All of the meats we got were good quality, and I loved their fish. They also had a buffet-style area where you can grab veggies, fish balls, and other hot pot ingredients that was very well-maintained and clean. I also love hot the hot pot includes unlimited soft drinks and dessert as well! The dessert was actually really good. Overall, great spot and I would definitely come back.

THIS is the place for your next hot pot! The variety was vast, the staff helpful, food both plentiful and delicious. My top bites were the lobster fish balls and the tiramisu at dessert time! So glad I came to try easy joy tonight. Will be back again!

Dim sum was delicious and authentic. The hot pot was also really good. The assortment of sauces and fresh ingredients was great. Desserts were plentiful and all flavorful. You can't go wrong with any of them. Service was ok...but expected for an Asian restaurant.

Olivia and Andrew You are the BEST! =)

My son came home from college for Thanksgiving weekend, and since he's only here for a week, I wanted to make the most of our time together. Originally, I planned for us to go to Hometown Hotpot & BBQ on Grand Street with my parents. But yesterday, November 21st, my dad mentioned a new spot on Mulberry Street--Easy Joy Dim Sum & AYCE Hot Pot--so we decided to give it a try.

It was my first time dining there, and the bright yellow signage instantly caught my eye from outside. When we walked in, the restaurant felt clean, warm, and relaxing--the exact atmosphere I always hope for. The hostess greeted us right away and kindly walked us to our seats near the buffet area, which turned out to be the perfect spot.

Our waitress, Olivia, came over quickly to take our drink orders. Since none of us drink alcohol, she suggested a few teas, and we went with jasmine tea. While we were looking over the menu for our hot pot broth, she noticed my dad was struggling to read the smaller print. Without hesitation, she went to the front and brought him a larger menu. I was impressed--her attention to detail really stood out.

Before we started eating, I headed to the restroom to wash my hands. I'm pretty picky about restroom cleanliness because I think it says a lot about how the rest of the restaurant is maintained. Honestly? 10/10. Clean, fresh, and clearly well taken care of.

Now, a funny moment. My dad--who always needs a little guiding--ordered the Mala broth and then told the server it was too spicy. Mala broth is supposed to be spicy! If you know my grandparents, you know how complicated they can be sometimes. But Olivia and our waiter Andrew handled it with so much patience. Maybe they have grandparents just like mine--LOL.

As for the food, everything was delicious. Since it's AYCE, we went all in: soft shell crab, fatty beef, shrimp, clams--you name it. The buffet section was loaded with options too: corn, bamboo, ramen noodles, potato noodles, beef balls, Fuzhou fish balls, and much more. Desserts were plentiful as well, from pineapple buns and egg tarts to cakes, yogurt, and all kinds of soda. And because my family loves beef, we ordered fatty beef over and over again--the portion size was perfect every time.

But the real highlight of the night wasn't just the food--it was the exceptional service from Olivia and Andrew. They checked on us constantly, cleared plates promptly, brought extra napkins, and refilled our drinks without us ever needing to ask. Their energy, attention to detail, and genuine care truly elevated the entire dining experience. They're not just great servers; they're leaders who make the restaurant shine.

Food can get you in the door, but it's people like Olivia and Andrew who make you want to come back. They're the heart of Easy Joy Dim Sum & AYCE Hot Pot, and I hope management recognizes what gems they have.

And just to put this out there--my son and Olivia definitely "connected." More to come... LOL.

Been there a bunch of times already. Love the hotpot!! Not a bad thing to say about it

As for the desserts... pls Add a soft serve machine please or ice cream instead??? The desserts are a waste of effort for whoever making them!!!! The cannoli is always soggy cause its prefilled and everything else is wasted.

went for a traditional dim sum breakfast and was not disappointed! food came quickly, was hot and fresh. the waitress was so sweet, literally an angel. very attentive and kind. the space is nice and clean. I would love to come back to try their hotpot!! thank you

My boyfriend and I have been raving about this place all day!!! 

SO GOOD!!!! First of all, the broths were fantastic. Our server recommended the mushroom broth-- so good!!! We got the spicy one too. He also helped us pick our meats and his recs were amazing!! I loved the fatty beef option, but tbh you can't go wrong. The crab and fish balls were my boyfriends fav to try in our broths! It was so fun picking all of our stuff and they had a bunch of sweet treat options too! 

The ambiance was so fun-- music was great. Not too loud, and a great spot for a date or friend group hangout! 

THE BEST PART -- our server and the hostess!!!! Hao was the best-- he was seriously so sweet, was super patient with our questions about the options, and gave us awesome recommendations. I thought everyone was really nice. They all made an effort to be readily available, were constantly bringing utensils and napkins to the table, and always were refilling our water!! They also were super funny and friendly which was a bonus.
Delicious food! Fun atmosphere.! Olivia gave us great service and was  very friendly!

I wound up here for a birthday dinner, and in the guest of honor's defense, it looked like Easy Joy was still offering AYCE dim sum.

Nope.

We were bamboozled. Or bam-bao-zled? 

They admitted they had lost way too much money offering AYCE dim sum, so now it's $2/dish if you get the premium AYCE hot pot options. Sigh. Not terribly expensive, but certainly not as ideal as, well, AYCE. So we got a few dishes just to try them out, and frankly, they were mid at best. Save your $2. You can buy a quarter cup of coffee with it.

As for the hot pot, the quality was fine. The Pork Collagen, Coconut Chicken and Tom Yum broths were all fine. The plant ingredients--which you pick out yourself via shelves in the back--were fine. The meat/seafood ingredients--which you order from your server--were fine.

But the actual experience of enjoying the hot pot was a sh*tshow for us. Our server decided early on she hated being assigned to wait on two long tables of 8, so she made herself just scarce enough to be inconvenient. 

And we unfortunately needed her often because Easy Joy is as well set up for hot pot as a hippo is for scuba diving. Real hot pot restaurants know to give you plenty of napkins, large ladles and slotted ladles, tabletop trash containers, water pitchers, etc. We had none of those with Easy Joy, so we were constantly flagging down a server to ask for more napkins, water, plates, etc.--which of course, endeared us more to them. 

I'll pay begrudging kudos to their wall of desserts that are part of the AYCE experience, but it's mostly just watered down mouses and dried up cakes, so....yay? Sugar calories with none of the deliciousness!

My $2? Walk the extra 3 blocks from this weirdly Little Italy-situated Chinese restaurant to actual Chinatown and dine at any number of the far superior hot pot restaurants there. You might even have enough napkins to make it through your first round!

Lunch review

Service was great. Extensive menu. We ordered a bunch of dim sum dishes and honestly, all of them were OK. Nothing really blew us away. We should have gotten the lunch special hot pot, which includes soft drinks, dessert, and would go back to try that but otherwise standard dim sum food in a elevated setting.

The food was great, superb selection of veggies and protein, as well as drinks. No alcohol served, but you are allowed to bring your own! Service was really attentive and understanding. The ambiance was really relaxed, the place is super clean and not too loud. Overall, I'd definitely come again!

Absolutely fantastic experience. Our waiter was so helpful and the dining ambience was outstanding. We chose the all you can eat option and the selection of meats and vegetables were mind baffling! I genuinely ate so much because each bite was so so good. After we had paid, we had the most lovely and genuine conversation with another waitress Olivia, and truly found one of the nicest staff teams in any restaurant I've ever been too. Next time I'm in NYC I will absolutely be coming back!

First time in NYC and this was our first meal in the city. I don't REGRET ITTT!!! The broth was fire-- I got the Sour Radish Duck Broth. The AYCE hot pot was just what I needed after a travel day. 

Ambience was fire. Playing all the jams.

Thank you to Olivia for making us feel so welcome and taken care of!!! Cheers!

First time in NYC and this was our first meal in the city. I don't REGRET ITTT!!! The broth was fire-- I got the Sour Radish Duck Broth. The AYCE hot pot was just what I needed after a travel day. 

Ambience was fire. Playing all the jams.

Thank you to Olivia for making us feel so welcome and taken care of!!! Cheers!

Oliva is THE BEST! Very attentive and makes your dining experience enjoyable. The ambiance was lively, still clam enough to hear each other speak. The food was amazing!! I'll be coming back anytime I get the craving for Dim Sum.

Food and service were AMAZING!! Visiting from SoCal and Iv had many hot pot experiences but this was by far my favorite!! I loved the seating and music! Olivia was an AMAZINGLY helpful and kind server!! Definitely have to come!

A newly opened hotpot spot nestled amongst Little Italy restaurants. We stopped by for their lunch specials and didn't have to wait to be seated. I guess this place is more popular on weekends and dinner time. I got the hotpot lunch special which came with 1 beef platter, 1 plate of vegetables/fish balls/sausages/noodles and choice of hot pot broth (pork collage or mushroom). My brother got the other option which came with 6 pork xiao long bao, choice of fried rice or noodles and a dessert. 

Larger tables of 8 can be divided into two tables of 4 by a small partition which is a thoughtful touch. Staff asked right away if we wanted hot tea or cold water. The tea comes in a small tea kettle and 2 tiny tea cups with a handle. 

Their current menu offers AYCE hotpot and a la carte dim sum. Their hot pot ingredients selection seemed very fresh, good quality and well stocked (fishballs, veggies, meats, noodles, rice cakes etc). They also had a nice dessert selection with tiramisu, puddings, fruits, cannoli etc. I liked that the desserts were offered in mini cups so that you could sample a little bit of everything (though I didn't get the chance to this time). The sauce station had a lot of sauces available as well as snacks like peanuts and preserved veggies. There are also plenty of soda drinks in their fridge.

My hotpot soup came out first. The pork bone brother came with giant pieces of pork bone with plenty of meat on it, a few pieces of corn, gingko berries, jujubes, mushrooms and green onions. It comes in a mini pot so I'm able to cook it on my own little stovetop. The beef slices were thin but not fatty at all. The combo platter was filled with so many vegetables and ingredients that I almost couldn't finish it all. My favorites were the fish roe fish ball, mushroom, corn and the napa cabbage. The platter came out exactly like how it looked on the promotional images on their windows. Staff even offered an apron just in case of hotpot splatters.

The fried noodles were an absolutely heaping portion as well. A few pieces of pork, carrots and cabbage stir fried with curly noodles. It was enough for two people to share. I think they steam their xiao long bao fresh when the order is placed because it was one of the last items to come out. The dessert was also so pretty! I loved the tiramisu cake and fruits toppings. 

I also went to the bathroom and it was clean and neat. I think they kept the previous restaurant's decor here because it didn't match the rest of the restaurant's interior design.
That was my first Hot Pot. It was delightful and delicious. Andrew, and everyone else, were pleasant and helpful. It was glorious.

Cute little joint in Little Italy. Stumbled here looking for Chinatown. Never had hotpot before so was wondering how this would go, but Hao was amazing at guiding us through the menu, letting us know there was two different menus and what we might like . Hao kept checking in on us during our dinner and asking if we were okay and other servers as well. To say my mom and I's first time at a hot pot place was amazing, it was. Thank you so much Hao!

Came here for dim sum and had such a good time. The food was solid, and the servers were funny and just the right kind of sassy. They definitely kept things entertaining.

Some highlights for me were the turnip cake, spare ribs, and siomai. Everything came out hot and tasty. I also loved that we got access to the hot pot sauce bar. Finally, a dim sum spot where you don't have to flag someone down for chili oil or water like you're signaling a plane.

They're not doing all-you-can-eat dim sum anymore, but the overall experience was still great. I'd definitely come back.
Delicious food and great buffet options! Our server was also super super nice. Definitely will be back

Visiting here with family, and the youngest in our group was craving dim sum. We found this spot and it's pretty legit! Place looks new, very clean, and the hostess, Olivia, and our server, Hao were both very nice. The portion size were great and price was very reasonable. We really enjoyed the black truffle dumplings and shu mai. We'd come back and try the hot pot if we're ever back in this area in the future.
Food, service, ambiance were great! Olivia was kind and so helpful. Will definitely come back!
Food was fresh and high quality. Staff (including the manager) were professional,  efficient, and pleasant. I will recommend this restaurant to my picky family and my friends.

Went here on a sat afternoon for the ayce dim sum, to find out they do not have that anymore. The food is good (I would stick to the steamed dishes) and fresh but nothing that blew me away taste wise. The soup dumplings were a hit but overall the food were lacking a bit more seasoning. Service was very attentive where trays and tea were constantly being taken care of. Nice and clean atmosphere!

Like mentioned the dim sum ayce is not available anymore. But we came for the hotpot.

Servers Johnny and Hao were great and attentive, really like the service that was given. The other staff was great as well.

The hotpot soups were great. The coconut chicken had coconut meat and I like that they gave you the chicken raw on the side for you to put it in yourself. We though the chicken was really good. Would be great if that was a menu option. The hotpot food are pretty standard, we were told the premium meat price were waived currently and that was great. No one seems to mention the soft drinks were included in the price which was a plus at least for me. 

It's not as pack now , went 6pm weekday? Which I kind of liked since we can have conversations without other noise and have space for ourselves. Will need to try the dim sum another time.
I came for dinner with my husband and we loved it! Totally recommended! Service was amazing too

Saw that this was a new dim sum and hot pot place in the Little Italy area that opened around a month ago. Arrived here on a Saturday late afternoon around 1:30 with couple of friends. We didn't make a reservation but we were seated right away. 

 Pricing & Value
FYI they no longer offer the ayce dimsum for $35 per person. However, with the AYCE hot pot ($43 per person), you have the option to order a la carte for $1.99 for dim sum. We did not choose the AYCE hot pot and only did the dim sum at the prices they had on their menu. Dim sum prices per dish ranges from $4.95- $10.95 (savory) and $2.95-$5.95 (sweet pastries/dessert). Not cheap, but the quality, portions, and overall experience made it 100% worth it.

 Ambience
The interior was modern -- think brick walls, plants, various types of  tile designs. Definitely seems like it's newly renovated. It's a cozy space without feeling cramped. On one side they have the fridge for some hot pot items, sauces, and drinks. 

‍ Service
Our server, Johnny and Olivia, were an absolute gem (other staff were great as well!). Both came to check up on use regularly and remained attentive and friendly. She answered all the questions I had such as birthday offer promotions! It was one of our friend's birthday so I thought why not ask? lol They do offer a free meal for that person's birthday if you choose the AYCE hot pot option and if it's the day of or 3 days before or after (call to confirm as that can change and I don't recall any other requirements). They also offered to sing a happy birthday song and came out with a neon sign! and a cute plushie! In addition to that, there is a raffle going on to win a Labubu! 

 Food & Drinks: 
Tried the following dim sum:
- Shrimp Dumplings
- Crab Meat Shumai
- Pork Dumplings
- Salted Egg Yolk Lava Bun
- Roast Pork Bun
- Chicken Feet
- Meat Ball
- Shrimp Rice Roll
- Beef Rice Roll
- Fried Turnip Cake
- Fried Sesame Ball
- Crispy Vegetarian Rice Roll
- Shanghai Soup Dumpling
- Shredded Roast Duck Dumpling

Amazing food, beautiful space, and wonderful staff. This is perfect for catching up with friends over good food! (We probably stayed for 4 hours and the staff were all so nice about it) Already planning to come back for dim sum or try their hotpot items!

September 16, 2025, I decided to have dim sum in this new place located at Little Italy ,NYC. I was not impressed at all with their food. The Shu Mai, Shrimp Rice Roll and Pork & Thousand, had no taste and was cold and not cooked properly. It was one of the worst Dim Sum I had. Will not be returning. When we arrived no one was at the restaurant, it was in the evening, another couple arrived later.

We were a party of 3 and came here for dinner last Friday with a reservation for 6pm.  Since this restaurant was recently opened, everything seemed clean and inviting. The hotpot burners were clean and functioning. 

I arrived at 6pm and was seated but my friends were going to be 15 minutes late.  Our hostess Olivia said, "no problem!".

We opted to have their hot pot and we eached picked the both of our choosing and were happy with our choices.  I had the Sour Radish Duck Broth which was very flavorful and I recommend.  My friends had the Wild Mushroom and Spicy Beef and they were happy with their selections.

The meats and seafoods that we ordered came out promptly by our server and were fresh and well prepared.  The veggies and other items, like tofus and noodles, are in a self-service refrigerated display and was well stocked.  I liked this self-service format for these items. 

Our server did give us a "90 minute for AYCE" alert so we started hurrying a bit.  I decided to ask our hostess, who had graciously checked on us a few times during our meal, if the time limit is strictly enforced and explained that we were having a reunion after a year apart.  Again, Olivia said, "no problem!" and we sat for almost another hour.  Fortunately, there weren't people lined up waiting to be seated though the restaurant was mostly full.

The food and service was good and I would not hesitate to come back!

A special shout-out for Olivia, with her charming smile, for helping us to have a very enjoyable reunion, along with the delicious food and good service!

I'm looking forward to trying their AYCE Dimsum!

Richard L

A new dim sum spot with a different proposition of ayce for $35, with the option for the usual a la carte ordering. I have had similar experiences before, but the main difference is that the dim sum here is fresh and delicious, and includes premium items such as truffle shrimp and crab soup dumplings! The price also includes soft drinks and desserts. Our favorite items were the fried crab claws, the soup dumplings, and truffle dumplings.

The service was very courteous and prompt. They also offer hotpot ayce for $43, which I would like to try some time! Will definitely be back!

Food is super high quality, the selection is affordable and really tasty. service is professional and helpful, the ambience is cozy and authentic. 

10/10 must come

Very tasty with their original soup base. We had the coconut chicken soup and sour radish duck soup and the sour one tasted exactly what i had back in hometown and it's the 1st i've seen across NYC. It's really worth the try and located in walkable neighborhoods that's cool for friends hangout too. They also have a large number of protein/vegetable/beverage/dessert options and are fresh and high quality. Will bring more friends back!! I've seen a couple people just dining alone and I feel it's a good place for a solo workday treat too loll The service is really nice and friendly and takes away dirty plates fast. The place is also clean and well maintained

I just had the dim sum buffet with a friend.  I discovered the place walking by when the establishment was giving out free spring roll samples.  Chen our server was super friendly, fast, and professional.   Service was excellent.   Hot pot will be tried in the future.

Positive experience from the time we walked in. 
Incredibly friendly yet professional service. 
Delicious  Dim Sum. 
Chen was especially helpful and kind. 
As was the gentleman giving out samples outside. 
Will definitely be back. 
Five star experience.

Cute little new dimsum/hotpot addition to the Chinatown area, with AYCE option at $35pp.

We came for the AYCE dim sum, and the dishes did not disappoint. Everything was very fresh, high in quality, and doesn't skimp in portion. Service was also very top noticed, and the place itself has very cute decor.

Will def come back again for dimsum and to try their hotpot option.

Amazing service. Great food.

We did the AYCE dimsum for $35/pp. There was a good amount of selection. Staff were extremely friendly and did not rush us.
From the food to the service. Everything was amazing. Shawn was our server and she was very nice and always tried to make our experience the best it could be!! Will come again.
Amazing experience, definitely recommended, the attention in this place is wonderful. Delicious food and great offer, eat all you can with $35. Amazing.

Loved this place! Olivia was the best server, but they are all good.  

We ordered the all u eat dim sum for $35.  You definitely have to get the black truffle dumpling. It was so delicious! 

Thanks ayce!

One of the best hotpot places I have eaten at. Definitely worth every penny. Not to mention the wide variety of seafood, meat and vegetarian selections. For only $1.99 each I can try Dim sum dishes that are worth $10+ aka the famous soup dumplings iykyk. Absolutely love. Tasty desserts as well. Our server was really sweet, great lighting in the restaurant as well. Nice job!
Dimsum bufet was worth it. So much food for $35. everything tasted so good and was fresh. Service was nice and very helpful.

All you can eat dim sum + hot pot = heaven. The fresh made classic xiao long bao is solid (yes, they bring in chefs from Shanghai) and even fancy black dumplings with a gold touch. Everything came out hot, fresh, and way better than your typical buffet vibe.
Hot pot had tons of soup bases and sauces, and the staff kept everything moving without us ever waiting long. Super fun spot to come with friends or family when you want to eat a lot and try a bit of everything.

Combining the best of both worlds - ayce hotpot and dimsum! The delicious broth sets this apart from other hotpot restaurants. They have the typical spicy and herbal broths, but the pickled radish duck broth is the winner here! Dimsum was impressive with steamed truffle shrimp dumplings, steamed scallop and shrimp dumplings, soup dumplings and peppers stuffed with fish and shrimp paste. While I was full already, I couldn't help but finish the creme brûlée and matcha pudding. $43 for AYCE hotpot and $1.99 for each dimsum dish OR $35 for AYCE dimsum.

Can't wait to enjoy Easy Joy again!
Great quality, delicious variety, & nice hospitality!

Loved the combo option because we wanted to try everything! We started with a couple of dim sum dishes which came out piping hot and very fresh - enjoyed the crunch on the duck spring rolls. It was my first time trying black truffle har gow - such a good combo when it's done right - so was the one with scallops and dou miao.

I liked the variety of special soup bases which are different from the other ayce hot pot spots. Our favorite was the flavorful duck broth - it was so good that we barely had to use any sauce! All the ingredients were high quality with a wide selection of fresh veggies, seafood, noodles, sauces and meats (esp the wagyu beef).  They had many options for beverages and dessert which are included too!

Thanks to the wonderful staff for their friendly and quick service. They were very helpful and attentive.  I also enjoyed the spacious, comfy booths and nice ambience. We had a great time and look forward to going back!

2 things I love. Hot pot and dim sum and now theres a restuarant that fulfills my dreams. Lol. 

They have some unique dishes I've never seen before for both dim sum and hotpot. My favorite broth was the sour radish duck broth. Super rich and flavorful that the soup base can stand alone as your hotpot sauce. Everything was so fresh and I like how you can self serve for the none meat items for hotpot. There is also an appetizer station, dessert and drink station which is a plus. 

For the dim sum, I say try it all. It's true to its picture and they dont skimp out on the ingredients.  I was able to taste the seafood. Super flavorful and juicy. The portion size is amazing too. 

Service was amazing, they made sure we understand the menu and the food came out promptly.
The food was awesome , the waiters are impeccable, the atmosphere in the store is lovely.
Amazing variety and fresh flavors! The hot pot broth was rich and flavorful, and the dim sum was perfectly cooked. Great service and a fun, all-you-can-eat experience--will definitely be back!
